unit.title: Install distribution panels, metering sockets, terminal mains and meter earthing systems

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A new house in Mandeville will have a 220 V water heater, two 220 V air conditioners and a 220 V stove, plus 110 V lights and sockets. What should you prepare first, to choose the panel and main breaker?
options: A sketch of where the client wants the furniture placed
A load schedule listing each circuit and its current
A price list from two electrical suppliers in the town
The meter number of the house next door, for reference

questions.stem: A load schedule needs 34 circuit ways. The specification asks for at least 20% spare ways. Which is the smallest panel that meets this?
options: 36-way
40-way
30-way
42-way

questions.stem: Why is the power company contacted early when planning a new service position?
options: It sets the meter position, the service size and its own rules
It installs the distribution panel and all the branch circuits
It carries out the government electrical inspection itself
It chooses which electrician is allowed to wire the house

questions.stem: You are to replace a damaged main breaker in a house panel. Why can you NOT make the job safe just by switching off and locking that main breaker?
options: A main breaker cannot be fitted with any kind of lock
The branch breakers would still feed the busbar
Its incoming terminals stay live from the meter
The earth bar would carry the full supply voltage

questions.stem: Before a panel change, the power company disconnects the supply at an agreed time. What must you still do before starting work?
options: Start removing the old panel while the crew is still on the way
Ask a neighbour to keep an eye on the meter for you
Prove dead at the incoming terminals with a checked tester
Switch off every branch breaker and begin straight away

questions.stem: A 220 V water heater is rated 4 400 W. What current does it draw?
options: 2 A

questions.stem: In a 110/220 V panel, L1 carries 110 V loads of 28 A and L2 carries 110 V loads of 12 A. A 10 A, 110 V circuit is moved from L1 to L2. What are the new line currents?
options: L1 38 A, L2 2 A

questions.stem: L1 carries 110 V loads of 20 A and L2 carries 110 V loads of 14 A, all simple heating and lighting. About what current flows in the neutral?
options: 6 A
0 A

questions.stem: Why does sharing the 110 V circuits evenly between L1 and L2 help the installation?
options: It lowers the neutral current and evens the load on each line
It raises the voltage on every socket outlet to 220 V for heavy loads
It lets each breaker carry twice its rated current safely
It removes the need for an earth on the 110 V circuits

questions.stem: After diversity, the maximum demand on the busier line is 72 A. Main breakers come in 60 A, 70 A, 100 A and 150 A, with the service and terminal mains sized to suit. Which is the best choice?
options: 60 A, because not every load runs at the same time
70 A, because it is the size nearest to the figure
100 A, the next standard size above the demand
150 A, so that there is plenty of room to spare

questions.stem: The power company gives the prospective fault current at a shop's service position as 10 kA. The main breaker is marked with a 6 kA breaking capacity. What does this mean?
options: The breaker is suitable, because it trips at 6 kA
It may not break the fault safely; use a higher rating
The breaker will trip too often and must be smaller
The 6 kA figure only applies to the 110 V circuits

questions.stem: Terminal mains 12 m long carry 80 A. The cable data gives 2.5 mV per amp per metre. What is the voltage drop?
Why are terminal mains sized for the main breaker's rating, not just for the load measured today?
options: So the cable is cheaper to buy in bulk lengths
So the panel door closes more easily over them
So the meter records the energy more accurately
The breaker lets that current flow without tripping

questions.stem: Aluminium terminal mains are to be connected to a main breaker. Which method is correct?
options: Any terminal, tightened as hard as possible, with any grease
Terminals rated for aluminium, anti-oxidant, maker's torque
Copper lugs squeezed on with pliers and then taped over
Ends soldered solid and then pushed into the terminal

questions.stem: A client wants the new panel inside a bathroom cupboard next to the shower. What is your best advice?
options: Agree, but fit a plastic bag over the panel to keep it dry
Agree, as long as the cupboard door is always kept shut
Advise a dry, easy-to-reach place outside the bathroom
Agree, and mount it lower so that it is easier to reach

questions.stem: A garage sub-panel is fed from the house's main panel. A trainee has bonded the neutral bar to the earth bar in the sub-panel. What is the problem?
options: Neutral current can flow on earth paths and metal parts
The sub-panel then needs no earth conductor of its own
The breakers in the sub-panel will not fit the busbar
The garage lights will now run at 220 V instead of 110 V

questions.stem: A surge protective device (SPD) is fitted in the main panel. Why must its leads be kept as short and straight as possible?
options: So that the panel door can close over the SPD
Long leads add voltage in a surge, so protection is less
So that the SPD uses less energy while it is idle
Long leads would make the SPD trip the main breaker

questions.stem: Why is a GFCI (RCD) breaker chosen for circuits feeding outdoor sockets and bathrooms?
options: It trips on small leakage currents that could pass through a person
It lets the circuit carry more current than a normal breaker of that size
It keeps the voltage steady when large motors start up
It stops lightning surges from entering the circuit

questions.stem: An outdoor meter socket is mounted on a block wall in the sun and rain. Which detail best keeps water out of it?
options: Bring every conduit into the top with plain indoor connectors
Drill extra drain holes along the sides of the socket
Tape over the gap round the cover after the meter is fitted
Use rainproof hubs and the entries the maker approves

questions.stem: Why is the metal enclosure of the meter socket connected to the earthing system?
options: So the power company can read the meter from a distance
So the meter disc turns more smoothly and quietly
So a fault to the enclosure cannot leave it live
So the neutral current can return through the case

questions.stem: Two extra earth rods are added to lower the earth electrode resistance. Why must they be spaced well apart, not driven close together?
options: Rods close together would rust each other in damp soil
Rods close together are hard to fit with clamps
Rods close together share the same soil, so add little
Rods close together would carry the neutral current

questions.stem: When testing an earth electrode with a three-terminal earth tester, why are readings taken with the potential spike at a few positions?
options: To find which spike has the best clamp on it
To make the test go faster on rocky ground
To use up the tester's battery more evenly
To confirm the readings agree and the spikes are far enough out

questions.stem: Before an earth electrode is disconnected from the main earthing terminal for testing, what must be true?
options: The installation is isolated, so nothing live is left unearthed
The neutral bar has been taken out of the panel and stored in a safe place
The meter has been removed by the electrician
The rod has been watered every day for a week

questions.stem: Where should the main bonding conductor be connected to an incoming metal water pipe?
options: At any tap inside the kitchen or bathroom
Near where the pipe enters the building
On a plastic section of the pipe
On the cover of the water meter

questions.stem: Why must a 220 V air conditioner circuit use a two-pole breaker (or breakers with a tied handle), not two separate single-pole breakers?
options: Both lines switch off together, so no line is left live
Two single breakers would put 440 V across the air conditioner
Two-pole breakers do not need to be labelled
Single-pole breakers cannot be used at 220 V

questions.stem: You supervise trainees terminating conductors in a panel. How do you check the terminals are tight to specification?
options: Pull hard on each wire by hand to see if it moves
Check them with a torque screwdriver set to the maker's value
Tighten every screw as hard as the screwdriver will go
Look for a shiny mark on each screw head as proof

questions.stem: Why are conductors in a panel dressed neatly along the sides, not across the front of the breakers?
options: So that they can carry a higher current
So that the earth bar is no longer needed
So breakers can be seen, reached and changed safely
So that the panel can be mounted upside down if space is tight

questions.stem: A metal conduit enters a metal panel through a knockout. Which fitting protects the cables and keeps the earth path of the conduit?
options: A rubber grommet pushed into the knockout
Insulating tape wrapped round the hole edge
A plastic cable tie round the conduit end
A conduit connector with locknut and bushing

questions.stem: Which label is needed on a sub-panel that is fed from a main panel in another building?
options: The date on which the sub-panel was bought
The name of the trainee who fitted it
The power company's account number
Where its supply can be isolated

questions.stem: Before the dead tests on a new panel, which inspection should be done?
options: Switch on each breaker in turn with its load connected
Plug a lamp into every socket outlet to see it light
Check sizes, connections and labels against the drawings
Ask the power company to fit the meter for a trial

questions.stem: Why is the protective conductor continuity test done before the insulation resistance test on a new installation?
options: It warms up the cables so that the insulation reads higher
Later tests to earth rely on a proven earth path
The insulation tester cannot be used on new cables at all
It is the only one of the tests that the inspector accepts

questions.stem: An insulation resistance test between line and earth on one new branch circuit gives a very low reading. What should you do next?
options: Split the circuit to find the fault before going on
Record the reading and ask for the inspection anyway, as planned
Repeat the test at a lower voltage until it passes
Swap over line and neutral and test again

questions.stem: Why is polarity checked on every 110 V circuit before the installation is connected?
options: So that the meter turns forwards and not backwards
So switches and breakers break the line, not the neutral
So that the earth rod stays damp in the dry season
So that the circuit uses less energy each month

questions.stem: The inspector's report on your new installation lists two faults. What is the right course of action?
options: Ask the power company to connect now, and fix the faults later
Fix only the fault that is cheaper, and leave the other
Explain to the client that small faults do not matter
Correct both, retest, and ask for a re-inspection

questions.stem: A client wants to add circuits next year. Which records help most in deciding whether the panel and service can take them?
options: The receipt for the panel from the supplier
A photo of the meter dial on the day of connection
The load schedule and the circuit schedule
The attendance sheet of the team that did the work

questions.stem: You lead three trainees installing a panel. When should you check their terminations?
options: At agreed hold points, before the covers go on
Only after the power company has connected it
Only if the government inspector finds a fault
Never, because trainees check their own work

questions.stem: The power company is about to reconnect a service your team has worked on. Where should the team be?
options: Inside the panel, giving the busbar a final check
Holding the meter steady in its socket
Clear of the panel, with covers on and tools out
On the roof, watching the service drop being fitted

questions.stem: Terminal mains run from an outdoor meter socket through the wall to an indoor panel. Why is the conduit sealed where it passes from outside to inside?
options: To stop water, insects and damp air reaching the panel
To stop the conductors from moving while they are being tightened
To stop the conduit from being connected to earth
So that the meter can be read from inside the house

questions.stem: How is the size of the earthing conductor from the main earthing terminal to the earth rod decided?
options: Use whatever is the smallest cable left in the store
From the service size and the specification's table
Make it the same as the smallest branch circuit
Size does not matter, since it carries no current

questions.stem: The earthing conductor is clamped to the rod below ground level in a pit. Why must the clamp be rated for direct burial?
options: So that it can be painted the right colour
So that it can be tightened by hand later
So that the power company can remove it
So it does not corrode and loosen in soil

questions.stem: L1 feeds 110 V circuits of 15 A, 12 A and 8 A. L2 feeds 110 V circuits of 10 A, 9 A and 6 A. All are heating and lighting loads. What is the neutral current?
A client's existing panel has no spare ways, and a new 220 V circuit is needed. What is the best solution?
options: Connect two circuits under one breaker terminal
Fit the new breaker into the main breaker's slot
Tap the new cable onto the panel's main lugs
Check the load, then fit a larger panel or a sub-panel

questions.stem: A guest house in Ocho Rios needs its main panel replaced. How should the outage be planned?
options: Start straight away and tell the guests afterwards
Agree a time with the owner and power company, and warn guests
Do it at night with torches so that nobody notices
Keep part of the old panel live so the guests have power

questions.stem: A standby generator is to feed a guest house's main panel during outages. What must be fitted so it cannot feed back into the power company's lines?
options: A larger main breaker
A surge protective device
An approved changeover (transfer) switch
A second earth rod beside the first

questions.stem: What should you explain to the client when you hand over a new panel?
options: How to change breakers while the panel is still live
How to switch off safely and what each breaker feeds
How to remove the meter seal to read the meter
How to bypass a breaker that keeps on tripping

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: A 220 V air conditioner is rated 3 080 W. How many amperes does it draw?
L1 carries 110 V loads of 26 A and L2 carries 110 V loads of 18 A, all heating and lighting. What current, in amperes, flows in the neutral?
Terminal mains 10 m long carry 100 A. The cable data gives 3 mV per amp per metre. What is the voltage drop, in volts?
What is the name of the conductor that runs from the main earthing terminal to the earth rod?
What do the letters SPD stand for?
What two-word name is given to the conductors that run from the meter socket's load terminals to the main breaker?
A 220 V circuit feeds a 5 500 W heater. What current does it draw, in amperes?
What word describes the allowance made in a load calculation because not every load runs at full power at the same time?
Which test instrument applies about 500 V DC to check that the insulation of a new installation is sound?
What is the name of the breaker that switches both lines of a 220 V circuit at the same time?
In what unit is the resistance of an earth electrode measured?
What is the name of the switch that connects a building either to the mains or to a standby generator, but never to both at once?
A panel needs 30 ways for its circuits, plus 20% spare. How many ways is that in total?
What is the name of the loop of conductor left below the weatherhead so that rain runs off before it reaches the service entrance?
What is the name of the pre-cut disc in a panel enclosure that is punched out to let a conduit or cable in?

essays.stem: A new house in Mandeville has these loads: a 3 300 W water heater, two 2 200 W air conditioners and a 6 600 W stove, all at 220 V. The 110 V lighting and socket circuits come to 25 A on L1 and 20 A on L2 after diversity. Use the figures as given, with no further diversity. Work out the current on each line and the neutral current, and choose a main breaker from 60 A, 100 A and 150 A. Explain your choice.
essays.modelAnswer: The 220 V loads draw current on both lines. Water heater: 3 300 ÷ 220 = 15 A. Each air conditioner: 2 200 ÷ 220 = 10 A, so 20 A for two. Stove: 6 600 ÷ 220 = 30 A. Together the 220 V loads give 15 + 20 + 30 = 65 A on each line. Adding the 110 V loads, L1 carries 65 + 25 = 90 A and L2 carries 65 + 20 = 85 A. The 220 V loads do not use the neutral, so the neutral carries only the difference between the 110 V loads: 25 − 20 = 5 A. The busier line carries 90 A, so a 60 A main breaker is too small. The 100 A breaker is the next size above 90 A and is the right choice, as long as the service and terminal mains are rated for 100 A. A 150 A breaker would need larger conductors and would not protect 100 A terminal mains. I would record the calculation in the load schedule.
markingPoints: Works out each 220 V load current correctly (15 A, 10 A each, 30 A)
Adds them correctly to give 90 A on L1 and 85 A on L2
Works out the neutral current as 5 A, explaining that 220 V loads do not use the neutral
Chooses 100 A and explains why 60 A and 150 A are wrong
Links the choice to the service and terminal mains rating and records it

essays.stem: You are to lead the replacement of the main panel at an occupied guest house in Ocho Rios. Explain how you would plan and carry out the isolation and the changeover safely.
essays.modelAnswer: I would survey the old panel and record every circuit, then prepare the new panel and a circuit schedule. I would agree a date and time with the owner so guests are warned and fridges and computers are protected, and book the power company to disconnect the supply, because the incoming terminals stay live even with the main breaker off. On the day, after the power company disconnects, I would lock off and tag where the Centre's or company's procedure says, then prove dead at the incoming terminals and every busbar with an approved tester checked on a proving unit before and after. Only then would the team remove the old panel, labelling each circuit. We would fit the new panel, connect the terminal mains and circuits to torque, and do the dead tests: continuity, insulation resistance and polarity. After the inspection the inspector and power company approve, the supply is restored by the power company, and I would hand over the updated schedule.
markingPoints: Surveys and records circuits and prepares the new schedule
Agrees the outage with the owner and books the power company disconnection, knowing the incoming side stays live
Locks off, tags and proves dead at the incoming terminals with a tester checked before and after
Labels circuits, installs to torque and carries out dead tests
Supply restored only after approval, by the power company; hands over updated records

essays.stem: A new house is being built on dry, rocky ground in St. Elizabeth. Describe how you would install and test the meter earthing system, and what you would do if the earth electrode resistance is too high.
essays.modelAnswer: I would check the site plan and ask about buried pipes and cables before choosing the rod position, close to the meter but clear of foundations and paths. I would drive a copper-bonded rod fully into the ground, or set it in an inspection pit, and fix the earthing conductor to it with a clamp rated for burial. The conductor would run in one length, without joints, to the main earthing terminal, and be protected by conduit where it could be damaged. With the installation not connected to a supply, I would test the electrode with a three-terminal earth tester, placing the test spikes in a straight line well away from the rod and taking readings with the potential spike at a few positions to confirm they agree. Dry, rocky soil often gives a high reading. I would then drive extra rods, spaced well apart and bonded together, or use a longer or deeper electrode, and test again. I would record every result and the final value for the inspection.
markingPoints: Checks for buried services and chooses a suitable rod position
Drives the rod fully and uses a burial-rated clamp and a continuous, protected conductor
Tests with the installation not connected, using a three-terminal tester correctly
Explains why rocky, dry soil gives a high reading and adds spaced, bonded rods or deeper electrodes
Retests and records the results

essays.stem: During an inspection you find that a sub-panel in an outbuilding has its neutral and earth bars joined, and no separate earth conductor runs back to the main panel. Explain the dangers and how you would correct it.
essays.modelAnswer: The neutral and earth should be joined at one place only, the main service position. In a sub-panel they must be separate, with a separate earth conductor run back to the main panel's earth bar. Here, normal neutral current will share the earth paths, so metal parts such as conduit, the panel case and appliance frames carry current and can have a voltage on them. If the neutral to the outbuilding breaks, the metal parts can rise towards line voltage, which could kill someone. GFCI (RCD) devices may also trip for no clear reason. To correct it, I would plan an outage, isolate the feeder at the main panel, lock off, tag and prove dead with a checked tester. I would remove the neutral-earth bond in the sub-panel, install a correctly sized earth conductor from the main panel to the sub-panel earth bar, and move all circuit earths to the earth bar. Then I would test continuity, insulation resistance and polarity, and record the work.
markingPoints: States neutral and earth are joined only at the main service position
Explains neutral current on earth paths and voltage on metal parts
Explains the danger if the neutral is lost, and nuisance tripping
Isolates safely, removes the bond and installs a separate earth conductor
Tests and records the correction

essays.stem: Explain the points you would consider when choosing the main breaker and the protective devices for a new shop's distribution panel.
essays.modelAnswer: First, the rating: the main breaker must be at least the maximum demand from the load calculation, and no larger than the service and terminal mains can carry, because it protects those conductors. Second, the breaking capacity: it must be at least the prospective fault current the power company gives, or it may fail to clear a short circuit safely. Each branch breaker is rated to protect its cable and suit its load, and two-pole breakers are used for 220 V circuits so both lines open together. The breakers should be chosen so a fault on a branch circuit trips that breaker, not the main one. GFCI (RCD) protection is used for outdoor sockets, wet areas and where the specification asks. A surge protective device is wise in Jamaica, where lightning is common, with short leads. All devices must be the type made for that panel, and spare ways allowed for growth.
markingPoints: Main breaker rating matched to maximum demand and to the service and terminal mains
Breaking capacity at least the prospective fault current
Branch breakers sized to cable and load, two-pole for 220 V; branch trips before main
GFCI (RCD) and surge protection where needed
Devices made for that panel, with spare ways

essays.stem: Terminal mains will run 18 m from the meter socket to a 100 A main breaker. Cable A is rated 90 A with a voltage drop of 1.8 mV per amp per metre. Cable B is rated 115 A with 1.4 mV per amp per metre. The specification allows a 2% voltage drop at 220 V. Choose the cable, showing your working, and describe how you would install it.
essays.modelAnswer: The terminal mains must carry at least the 100 A main breaker rating. Cable A is rated only 90 A, so it is too small whatever its voltage drop. Cable B is rated 115 A, which is enough. The allowed voltage drop is 2% of 220 V = 4.4 V. For cable B, the drop is 1.4 × 100 × 18 = 2 520 mV = 2.52 V, which is under 4.4 V, so cable B passes. I would choose cable B. To install it, I would run suitable conduit from the meter socket's load side to the panel by the shortest practical route, with rainproof hubs outside and a seal where the conduit passes into the building. The conductors are pulled in without damage, kept in one length with no joints, and identified at both ends. They are terminated on the meter socket's load terminals and the main breaker with the right lugs and torque, using anti-oxidant on aluminium. The supply terminals are left for the power company.
markingPoints: Rejects cable A because its rating is below 100 A
Works out the allowed drop (4.4 V) and cable B's drop (about 2.5 V) correctly
Chooses cable B with a clear reason
Describes the conduit route, rainproof entries and seal, with no joints in the conductors
Terminates on the load side to the correct torque and leaves the supply terminals for the power company

essays.stem: Write the inspection and test plan your team will follow on a new panel, meter socket and earthing system before the government inspection, and explain what you will do with any result that fails.
essays.modelAnswer: The plan starts with a visual inspection while everything is dead and not connected: the meter socket is level, firm and weatherproof, with its supply terminals untouched; conduit and entries are sealed; the panel is in a dry, reachable place; conductor sizes and breaker ratings match the drawings; terminations are torqued; neutral and earth are joined only at the main service position; and labels and the circuit schedule are complete. Then the dead tests, in order: continuity of protective and bonding conductors, insulation resistance of each circuit with electronic equipment disconnected, and polarity. The earth electrode resistance is measured with the three-terminal tester. Each test is given to a named member, and I check the results. Any failed result is investigated, the fault found and corrected, and the test repeated and recorded. Nothing is passed for inspection until every result is acceptable and the records are signed.
markingPoints: Lists the visual inspection items for meter socket, panel and earthing
Puts the dead tests in the right order with electronics disconnected
Includes the earth electrode test
Assigns and checks the tests as the leader
Investigates, corrects and retests failures, and signs the records before inspection

essays.stem: You supervise three trainees installing a distribution panel and terminal mains on a building site. Describe how you would brief, supervise and check their work.
essays.modelAnswer: Before work starts I would hold a short briefing: the drawing, the panel position, the order of work, the hazards and the safety rules, including that the supply side of the meter socket is the power company's and no one connects to it. I would give each trainee clear tasks, such as mounting the panel, running the conduit or terminating circuits, and check that they have the right tools, including a torque screwdriver. I would set hold points where I check the work before the next step: the panel fixed level and firm, the conduit and bushings before conductors go in, and the terminations before the cover goes on. At each hold point I would check sizes, connections, torque, neutral and earth arrangement and labelling, and explain any fault so the trainee learns. I would watch the dead tests and check the records, and finish with a short review of what went well and what to improve.
markingPoints: Briefs the team on drawings, order of work, hazards and the power company's side
Gives clear tasks and checks tools
Sets hold points before the next step
Checks quality at each hold point and coaches the trainees
Watches the tests, checks records and reviews the job

essays.stem: Explain why 110 V loads should be balanced between L1 and L2 in a 110/220 V panel, and what can happen to the 110 V equipment if the shared neutral breaks.
essays.modelAnswer: In a 110/220 V system, the two lines are each 110 V to the neutral, and 220 V between them. The 110 V loads on L1 and L2 send their return current through the shared neutral, but the currents work against each other, so the neutral carries only the difference. When the loads are balanced the neutral current is small, the lines share the load evenly, and the voltage stays steady. If one line is loaded much more than the other, that line and the neutral carry more current, so they heat more and the voltage on that side falls. If the shared neutral breaks, the 110 V loads on L1 and L2 are left in series across 220 V. The side with less load gets more than 110 V and the side with more load gets less. Lamps, TVs and electronics can be damaged or catch fire. This is why the neutral must be well terminated and the loads balanced.
markingPoints: Explains 110 V line to neutral and 220 V line to line
Explains that the neutral carries the difference between the 110 V loads
Explains the benefits of balance (less neutral current, even loading, steady voltage)
Explains that a broken neutral puts the 110 V loads in series across 220 V
Explains the result: over-voltage on the lightly loaded side and damage or fire

essays.stem: Explain why a standby generator must be connected to a building through a changeover switch, and describe how you would plan its connection to an existing panel.
essays.modelAnswer: Without a changeover switch, a generator connected to a building's wiring can feed power back through the meter into the power company's lines. A line worker who has isolated the line could be killed, and when the mains comes back the generator can be damaged. A changeover switch connects the building to the mains or the generator, never both. To plan the job, I would check the generator's output and the loads it must feed, and decide whether it feeds the whole panel or a sub-panel of essential circuits. I would choose a changeover switch rated for the load, place it between the meter and the panel or the essential sub-panel, and plan the cable, the generator's earthing and the neutral arrangement as the maker and specification say. I would plan the outage, with the power company disconnecting the supply, and safe isolation with lock, tag and proving dead. After dead tests and inspection, the installation is approved before use.
markingPoints: Explains back-feed and the danger to line workers
States that the changeover switch connects to one source only
Checks generator size, loads and the essential circuits
Places and rates the changeover switch correctly, with earthing and neutral as specified
Plans the outage, safe isolation, tests and approval

practical1.title: Plan, install and pre-inspect a meter socket, main panel and sub-panel with terminal mains on a training bay
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a drawing and a list of loads for a small building, and the Centre's training bay with a meter socket, a main panel, a sub-panel and conduit. The bay is never connected to a supply. As a group: (1) write a load schedule, work out the current on each line and the neutral current, choose the main breaker and branch breakers, and balance the 110 V circuits across L1 and L2; (2) write a circuit schedule and a short method statement with hold points; (3) mount the meter socket and panels plumb and firm, run conduit with the right connectors, bushings and rainproof entries; (4) install the terminal mains from the meter socket's load terminals to the main breaker, neutral and earth; the supply terminals are left empty and labelled 'Supply side: power company only'; (5) feed the sub-panel with a separate earth conductor and keep its neutral and earth bars apart; (6) terminate at least four branch circuit tails, including one two-pole breaker, to the maker's torque; (7) carry out an inspection checklist and the dead tests (protective conductor continuity, insulation resistance and polarity) and record them on a pre-inspection record. Each member leads one stage and the leader for each hold point gets the assessor's check before moving on. Photograph each stage and hand in all the documents.
materials: Training bay with meter socket, main panel, sub-panel and conduit (not connected to any supply)
Drawing and load list from the assessor
Main breaker, single-pole and two-pole branch breakers to suit the panel
Conductors for terminal mains, sub-main and branch tails, with lugs
Conduit connectors, locknuts, bushings and rainproof hubs
Torque screwdriver and wrench, strippers, crimping tool
Low-resistance ohmmeter and insulation resistance tester
Two-pole voltage tester and proving unit
Labels, circuit schedule, method statement and pre-inspection record forms
photos: The load schedule and balance calculation
Meter socket and panels mounted, with conduit and entries fitted
The supply terminals of the meter socket, empty and labelled
Terminal mains terminated on the load side and at the main breaker
Sub-panel showing separate neutral and earth bars and the earth conductor
Branch circuits terminated and dressed, before the covers go on
The dead tests being carried out, and the completed records
The finished bay with covers fitted and labels on
checklist: Worked out line and neutral currents correctly and balanced the 110 V circuits
Chose breaker ratings that match the loads and conductors
Mounted equipment plumb and firm, with correct conduit fittings and sealed entries
Left the meter socket supply terminals untouched and labelled
Kept neutral and earth separate in the sub-panel, with a separate earth conductor
Terminated conductors neatly to the maker's torque
Carried out and recorded the dead tests correctly
Led their stage clearly and checked work at the hold points
safety: The bay is never connected to a supply; only the instructor may energise anything
Never touch or connect to the supply terminals of the meter socket
Wear safety glasses when cutting conduit and stripping conductors
Discharge circuits after insulation resistance tests, as the tester's maker says
Lift panels with two people and keep the work area tidy

practical2.title: Install a two-rod meter earthing and bonding system, test it, and write an earthing report
practical2.brief: In the Centre's earthing practice area, the assessor gives the group a site plan showing a training board (not connected to any supply), buried services and a metal water pipe. As a group: (1) check the site plan for buried services and mark out positions for two rods, spaced as the assessor's instructions say; (2) drive the first rod, fit a burial-rated clamp and run the earthing conductor in one length, protected where shown, to the main earthing terminal on the board; (3) with the board isolated and the conductor disconnected, measure the electrode resistance with a three-terminal earth tester, taking readings with the potential spike at three positions; (4) drive the second rod, bond it to the first, and test again; (5) bond the metal water pipe near its entry point to the main earthing terminal, and test the continuity of all earthing and bonding conductors; (6) reconnect and check every connection; and (7) write a short earthing report with a sketch, the readings before and after the second rod, what they show, and any recommendation. Every member drives a rod, fixes a clamp or conductor, or takes a reading, and each records part of the report. Photograph each stage and hand in the report.
materials: Two copper-bonded earth rods and burial-rated clamps
Earthing and bonding conductor, conduit for protection, and a pipe bonding clamp
Rod driver or sledgehammer, and an inspection pit cover if used
Three-terminal earth tester with spikes and leads
Training board with a main earthing terminal and a metal water pipe (not connected to any supply)
Site plan from the assessor, tape measure, marker pegs
photos: The site plan checked and the rod positions marked
The first rod driven and the clamp fitted
The earth tester set up, with spikes in line
The second rod driven and bonded to the first
The water pipe bonding clamp and conductor
The continuity test and the completed readings
The finished earthing report with its sketch
checklist: Checked for buried services before driving rods
Drove rods fully and fitted burial-rated clamps firmly
Ran the earthing conductor in one length and protected it where needed
Set up the earth tester correctly and took readings at more than one spike position
Bonded the water pipe near its entry point
Tested continuity of earthing and bonding conductors correctly
Explained what the readings before and after the second rod show
Wrote their part of the report clearly and accurately
safety: Check for buried cables and pipes before driving rods or spikes
Wear safety boots, gloves and safety glasses when driving rods; keep others clear of the hammer
The board is never connected to a supply; disconnect the electrode only with the board isolated
Keep test leads tidy so no one trips over them
